subject: Hospitality
title: Wellness-Centered Design
description: A quick win: understand Wellness-Centered Design.

hook.text: The WELL Building Standard certifies buildings designed for human health—air quality, water purity, light, fitness.

buildup.text: WELL-certified hotels filter air to hospital-grade standards, use circadian lighting, and provide fitness equipment in every room.

discovery.text: Six Senses hotels embed wellness into architecture: yoga pavilions, organic gardens, sleep programs.

twist.text: Wellness design is becoming expected, not exceptional. Post-pandemic guests choose healthy buildings like they once chose views.

climax.text: The convergence of health, sustainability, and design is producing hotels that are genuinely good for people—not just comfortable.

punchline.text: Clean air, circadian light, in-room fitness. Hotels designed to heal, not just house.

quiz.question: What does the WELL Building Standard certify?
options: Buildings designed for human health—air quality, light, fitness, and well-being
